Use this guide only when all 21 active pills contain the same hormone dose, followed by a 7-day pill-free break. Do not use it for multiphasic, progestogen-only, 24+4, 26+2, continuous or emergency contraception.
How long since the first missed pill was due?
Where are you in the pack?
Take the late or missed pill as soon as possible, then take the remaining pills at the usual time. Taking two pills on the same day is allowed. Extra contraception is generally not needed.
Take the most recent missed pill now

Discard any earlier missed pills and continue the pack at the usual time. Avoid sex or use condoms until you have taken active pills correctly for 7 consecutive days. If you had unprotected sex in the previous 5 days, seek prompt advice about emergency contraception.

Discard any earlier missed pills and continue the pack at the usual time. Avoid sex or use condoms until you have taken active pills correctly for 7 consecutive days. Emergency contraception is usually unnecessary if the previous 7 pills were taken correctly.

Discard any earlier missed pills and finish the active pills in this pack. Skip the 7-day break and start a new pack the next day. Avoid sex or use condoms until you have taken active pills correctly for 7 consecutive days.
When does protection begin after starting for the first time?

As a cautious app rule, avoid sex or use condoms until you have taken active pills correctly for 7 consecutive days. If pregnancy cannot be excluded or you had unprotected sex before starting, speak to a clinician or pharmacist.
What if I start the next pack late?

Start the new pack as soon as possible and treat it like missed pills in week 1. Avoid sex or use condoms until you have taken active pills correctly for 7 consecutive days. Seek prompt advice if you had unprotected sex in the previous 5 days.
What if I vomit or have severe diarrhoea?

If it lasts under 48 hours, keep taking pills at the usual time; extra contraception is generally not needed. At 48 hours or more, follow the missed-pill rules. After recovery, use condoms until active pills have been taken correctly for 7 consecutive days. If this happens on days 15–21, skip the break and start a new pack.

This guide provides general information and does not replace your medicine leaflet or advice from a clinician or pharmacist. Different brands and regimens may have different instructions. Seek professional advice if you are unsure about your pill, pregnancy is possible, or emergency contraception may be needed. Combined pills do not protect against sexually transmitted infections.
Based on CDC U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations for Contraceptive Use (2024) and NHS combined-pill guidance (reviewed 2024).
